Instead of passing light through the sample, ATR relies on the evanescent wave that penetrates only a few micrometers into the medium at the crystal interface, effectively creating an extremely short path length that enables the measurement of "black" or highly scattering fluids without dilution. steps: 1. Survey commercially available sodium‑sensitive fluorescent dyes and select up to three candidates.
2. Prepare calibration standards in brine and record fluorescence spectra using the client’s excitation source.
3. Record Raman spectra of the same standards with a 90° back‑scattering probe.
4. Compare calibration performance (linearity, limit of detection) against ion‑chromatography reference.
5. Assess probe fouling and optical interference under realistic tank conditions.
6. Summarize results and recommend the most viable method for further scale‑up.
